investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GETs (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's own official programme day-list page and two individually-linked event detail pages. The day-list page is static HTML with no embedded JSON-LD, but each event detail page it links to embeds exactly one schema.org 'MusicEvent' JSON-LD block with name/startDate/endDate/location/performer/url.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.konzerthaus.de/en/programm (302-redirects to a dated day-list page, e.g. /en/programm/26-08-2026) returned static HTML with real <a href> links to individual event detail pages under /en/programm/{slug}/{id}. Fetching two of those linked event pages directly (no login, no JS execution) each exposed one clean <script type="application/ld+json"> MusicEvent block with name, startDate, endDate, location (venue address + room name), performer[], and url. This directly answers the investigation question at Level 1 — the day-list page supplies real event URLs, and each event URL supplies real structured MusicEvent data; no structural/browser escalation was needed to determine acquisition class.

venue_reference: Konzerthaus Berlin (major classical concert hall, Gendarmenmarkt, Mitte, Berlin — home of the Konzerthausorchester Berlin, with a substantial public symphony/chamber/family programme)

identity.notes: konzerthaus.de is the venue's own first-party domain (not a ticketing aggregator or third-party listing site) — the retained event page states its own address 'Gendarmenmarkt, 10117 Berlin, Deutschland' matching the venue's well-known public location, and the domain is independently corroborated by third-party reference sources found during discovery (Wikipedia, visitBerlin.de) as Konzerthaus Berlin's own official site, not merely asserted by this investigation.

site_classification.platform: Custom in-house CMS (no WordPress/Sanity/known-plugin fingerprint observed — static jQuery-driven front end, static.js build assets). The day-list/programme page itself does NOT embed JSON-LD, only static HTML links to individual event detail pages; each event detail page embeds its own single schema.org 'MusicEvent' JSON-LD block.

title.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'name' field (e.g. "Konzerthausorchester Berlin, Iván Fischer", "Espresso-Konzert").

start_date.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'startDate' field, an ISO 8601 local datetime with NO UTC offset (e.g. '2026-09-25T19:00') — honestly FLOATING_LOCAL, never upgraded to a UTC instant.

time.notes: Time-of-day portion of the same 'startDate' JSON-LD field.

end.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'endDate' field, same floating-local ISO shape as startDate.

venue_location.notes: Each event's JSON-LD 'location' object states 'address': 'Gendarmenmarkt , 10117 Berlin, Deutschland' directly (this uniquely identifies Konzerthaus Berlin as the physical building). 'location.name' is a sub-room within that building (e.g. 'Großer Saal', 'Kleiner Saal') rather than the literal venue name — the same room-within-venue pattern already accepted for Razzmatazz's numbered rooms in this project's own precedent, not a separate venue.

source_record_id.notes: No explicit JSON-LD 'identifier' field is exposed. This source's own event detail URL directly embeds a numeric id as the final path segment (e.g. '/en/programm/konzerthausorchester-berlin-ivan-fischer/12461' -> 12461), matching the site's own canonical link/permalink scheme (also restated verbatim in JSON-LD's own 'url' field) rather than a hash this investigation invented. Matches the documented 'permalink URL slug the source uses as its own canonical path' stability rule.

event_url.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'url' field, restating the exact canonical URL used to fetch that page.

price.notes: No 'offers'/price field present in either sampled JSON-LD block. Konzerthaus Berlin sells tickets through its own site (ticket links visible in surrounding page HTML) but no structured price was present in the retained JSON-LD itself — genuinely not collected at this level, not fabricated as absent.

blockers.description: Unlike Moog Barcelona's single-page array of 37 JSON-LD events, Konzerthaus Berlin exposes JSON-LD only per individual event detail page — the day-list page itself carries no JSON-LD, only plain <a href> links. A collector using the existing generic ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs module would need a first crawl step (enumerate event detail URLs from one or more day-list pages, which may themselves need day-by-day or month pagination) before applying the existing JSON-LD parser per event page. This is real but modest additional discovery work, not a new collector family.

reasons: Identity PROVEN on the venue's own first-party domain.
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved supported class, genuinely confirmed by two sampled event pages.
Two CONFIRMED public data paths retained (day-list HTML for URL discovery; event detail HTML for JSON-LD MusicEvent data).
title, start_date, end, venue_location, event_url all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own stable permalink/URL id scheme.
recommended_family JSON_LD, an already-existing, proven, reusable family (ingestion/json-ld/) — requires no new collector code, only a day-list crawl step ahead of the existing parser.
